detail.query: 무기/유기금속화학, 균일계 촉매, 기능성 고분자, 바이오매스에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Advanced Inorganic and Organometallic Chemistry (CHM450-01)
교과개요
This course explores the fundamental principles governing the structure, bonding, and reactivity of inorganic and organometallic compounds. Special emphasis is placed on the application of these principles to design homogeneous catalysts for sustainable chemical transformations. Students will investigate the electronic properties of transition metals, ligand field theory, and mechanistic pathways in catalytic cycles involving biomass-derived substrates. The curriculum bridges the gap between classical coordination chemistry and modern applications in functional polymer synthesis and bio-inspired catalysis.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to predict the geometry and electronic structure of complex metal centers, propose detailed mechanisms for homogeneous catalytic reactions including those utilizing renewable biomass feedstocks, and design ligand environments that tune reactivity for specific functional polymer applications. The course also aims to cultivate an understanding of how organometallic chemistry serves as a cornerstone for developing next-generation materials and green chemical processes.

---

Catalysis and Functional Materials from Biomass (MAT480-01)
교과개요
This interdisciplinary course focuses on the conversion of biomass into high-value functional materials through advanced catalytic strategies. Utilizing concepts from organometallic chemistry, students will examine homogeneous and heterogeneous catalytic systems designed for depolymerization, upgrading, and polymerization of bio-based monomers. The course delves into the synthesis of functional polymers with tailored properties derived from renewable resources and explores the integration of metal complexes into polymeric matrices to create smart materials. Practical sessions emphasize the characterization of catalysts and polymers to link molecular structure with macroscopic performance.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to evaluate catalytic systems for biomass valorization, synthesize or characterize functional polymers derived from renewable feedstocks, and analyze the relationship between metal-ligand interactions and catalytic efficiency in complex reaction environments. The course also aims to strengthen the ability to propose innovative solutions for sustainable material production by integrating knowledge of organometallic mechanisms with polymer science.

detail.query: 시간분해 엑스선 산란, 반응 메커니즘 연구, 단백질 구조동역학에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
시간분해 엑스선 산란 및 생체분자 동역학 (PHY598-01)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of ultrafast X-ray scattering techniques and structural biology, focusing on how matter evolves on femtosecond to nanosecond timescales. We will examine the fundamental principles of time-resolved diffraction and small-angle scattering, specifically tailored for studying protein folding pathways, conformational changes, and reaction mechanisms in real-time. The curriculum bridges the gap between condensed matter physics and biophysics, utilizing pump-probe methodologies to capture transient states that are invisible to static structural methods.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design experiments for time-resolved X-ray scattering, interpret dynamic structure factors to extract kinetic models of biomolecular reactions, and analyze data to reconstruct reaction mechanisms involving protein dynamics. The course aims to equip students with the theoretical framework to connect structural fluctuations with functional changes in biological systems.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 시간분해 산란의 물리적 기초 및 펌프-프로브 원리
2 주차: X-ray Diffraction 및 Small-Angle Scattering 이론 복습
3 주차: 단백질 접힘 (Folding) 과정에서의 구조 변화 분석 방법론
4 주차: 반응 메커니즘 연구 사례: 효소 촉매 작용의 초고속 관찰
5 주차: 펩타이드 결합 형성/파괴 과정의 동역학 모델링
6 주차: 실험 데이터 처리 및 시간 의존적 구조 인자 (Time-dependent Structure Factor) 해석
7 주차: 생체분자 내부 진동 모드와 집단 운동 (Collective Motion) 분석
8 주차: 시뮬레이션과 실험 데이터의 통합: 분자동역학 시뮬레이션 기초
9 주차: 액체 상태 단백질의 구조 동역학 및 수화층 효과 연구
10 주차: 막 단백질의 구조 변화와 기능적 연관성 탐구
11 주차: 최신 시간분해 엑스선 실험 시설 및 데이터 분석 툴 소개
12 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 반응 메커니즘 해석 실습

detail.query: 단백질화학, 화학생물학, 생화학에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
단백질화학 (BS305-01)
교과개요
This course explores the chemical principles underlying protein structure, function, and dynamics. We will examine how amino acid sequences fold into specific three-dimensional architectures and how these structures enable biological activities such as catalysis, signaling, and molecular recognition. The curriculum bridges classical biochemistry with modern structural biology techniques, emphasizing the relationship between sequence, structure, and function in a quantitative framework.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to predict secondary structure elements from primary sequences, interpret experimental data from X-ray crystallography and NMR spectroscopy, and apply thermodynamic concepts to analyze protein-ligand interactions. The course also aims to cultivate an understanding of how chemical modifications regulate biological processes and design simple experiments to investigate protein stability.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 단백질의 기본 구성 요소 및 아미노산 화학적 성질
2 주차: 펩타이드 결합 형성 및 1 차 구조 결정
3 주차: 단백질 접힘의 열역학 (안정성, 자유 에너지)
4 주차: 2 차 구조 (알파 나선, 베타 시트) 의 형성과 안정화 요인
5 주차: 3 차 구조 결정 방법론 (X 선 회절 및 NMR 원리)
6 주차: 단백질의 4 차 구조 및 올리고머 형성
7 주차: 효소의 기질 특이성 및 촉매 메커니즘
8 주차: 알로스테릭 조절 및 협동성 결합 현상
9 주차: 단백질 - 리간드 상호작용 및 친화도 분석 (Kd, ΔG)
10 주차: 구조 기반 약물 설계의 기본 원리
11 주차: 단백질 변성 및 재접힘 과정 연구
12 주차: 최신 화학생물학 기술 동향 및 사례 연구

detail.query: 다공성 금속유기구조체(MOFs) 합성 및 환경 분야 응용에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
다공성 금속유기구조체 (MOFs) 의 합성 메커니즘 제어 및 환경 정화, 가스 저장 등 응용 분야를 심층적으로 다루는 가상의 강의계획서입니다.

고체화학 및 재료공학개론 (MAT450-01)
교과개요
This course explores the design, synthesis, and functionalization of Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs), focusing on their unique porous structures and tunable chemical environments. We will cover reticular chemistry principles, solvothermal synthesis methods, post-synthetic modification techniques, and characterization strategies such as XRD, BET surface area analysis, and in situ spectroscopy. Special emphasis is placed on tailoring MOF properties for environmental applications, including heavy metal ion adsorption, organic pollutant removal from water, and carbon capture technologies.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design novel MOF architectures based on specific target functionalities, optimize synthesis conditions to control crystallinity and porosity, interpret structural characterization data, and propose innovative solutions for environmental remediation challenges using MOF-based materials.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 고체화학 및 다공성 물질의 기초 개념 (Zeolites vs. MOFs)
2 주차: MOF 의 구조적 설계 원리 및 리타큘러 화학 (Reticular Chemistry)
3 주차: 금속 노드와 유기 링커의 선택 및 조합 전략
4 주차: 용매열 합성법 (Solvothermal Synthesis) 과 반응 조건 최적화
5 주차: MOF 의 결정화 메커니즘과 결함 공학 (Defect Engineering)
6 주차: 포스트-합성 변형 (Post-Synthetic Modification) 기법
7 주차: 구조 분석 및 특성화 기술 (XRD, SEM/TEM, BET 등)
8 주차: 가스 흡착 및 저장 성능 평가 방법론
9 주차: 중금속 이온 제거를 위한 MOF 기반 수처리 시스템 설계
10 주차: 유기 오염물 분해 및 촉매적 응용 사례 연구
11 주차: 이산화탄소 포집 및 분리 기술에서의 MOF 활용
13 주차: 실제 환경 시뮬레이션 실험 및 데이터 분석 실습
14 주차: 지속 가능한 에너지 저장 소재로서의 MOF 가능성 탐구
15 주차: 최신 MOF 연구 동향 및 미래 전망 (Perovskites, COFs 등과의 비교)

detail.query: 유기화학, 유기금속화학, 촉매에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
유기금속촉매론 (ORG450-01)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of organic chemistry and organometallic catalysis, focusing on how transition metal complexes facilitate complex carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bond formations. We will examine fundamental concepts such as oxidative addition, reductive elimination, migratory insertion, and beta-hydride elimination within the context of modern synthetic methodology. The curriculum bridges the gap between mechanistic understanding and practical application in pharmaceutical synthesis, materials science, and sustainable energy conversion.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to predict reaction pathways for organometallic-catalyzed transformations, design synthetic routes utilizing cross-coupling reactions (e.g., Suzuki-Miyaura, Heck, Sonogashira) and C-H activation strategies, and evaluate catalyst ligand effects on selectivity and turnover frequency. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to critically analyze recent literature in catalysis and propose novel mechanistic hypotheses based on spectroscopic and kinetic data.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: Introduction to Organometallic Catalysis - Cycle of Catalytic Reactions (Oxidative Addition, Reductive Elimination)
2 주차: Fundamentals of Ligand Design - Electronic and Steric Effects (Tolman Parameters, Cone Angle)
3 주차: Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling Reactions I - Suzuki-Miyaura and Stille Couplings
4 주차: Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling Reactions II - Heck, Sonogashira, and Negishi Couplings
5 주차: Nickel-Catalyzed Transformations - Advantages and Limitations in C-C Bond Formation
6 주차: Copper-Catalyzed Ullmann-Type Reactions and Click Chemistry Applications
7 주차: Rhodium and Iridium Catalysis - Hydroformylation, Carbonylation, and Asymmetric Hydrogenation
8 주차: Platinum Group Metals in C-H Activation Strategies
9 주차: Mechanistic Elucidation of Organometallic Cycles - Kinetic Isotope Effects and Linear Free Energy Relationships
10 주차: Ligand Accelerated Catalysis and Single-Atom Catalysts
11 주차: Photoredox Catalysis and Dual-Catalytic Systems
12 주차: Green Chemistry in Organometallic Catalysis - Atom Economy and Waste Reduction
13 주차: Case Studies in Industrial Applications - Pharmaceutical Synthesis and Polymerization
14 주차: Frontiers in Research - Bioorthogonal Catalysis and Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction
15 주차: Comprehensive Review and Final Project Presentations

detail.query: 펨토초 이미징, 초고속 동역학, 차세대 반도체 물성 분석에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
펨토초 광물리 (PHY501-01)
교과개요
This course explores the frontiers of ultrafast science and technology, focusing on the manipulation and observation of matter on femtosecond timescales. Utilizing advanced laser physics and attosecond spectroscopy techniques, students will investigate the fundamental mechanisms governing electron dynamics, lattice vibrations, and chemical reactions in real-time. The curriculum bridges the gap between condensed matter physics and semiconductor engineering, providing a deep understanding of how ultrafast pulses can probe and control material properties for next-generation device applications.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design experiments involving femtosecond laser systems, analyze transient absorption and pump-probe data to extract carrier dynamics, and interpret spectroscopic signatures in complex semiconductor heterostructures. The course aims to cultivate expertise in characterizing ultrafast charge transport, hot-carrier relaxation, and phase transitions essential for developing high-speed optoelectronic devices and novel quantum materials.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: Introduction to Ultrafast Science and Attosecond Physics
2 주차: Fundamentals of Femtosecond Laser Systems and Pulse Compression
3 주차: Nonlinear Optics for High-Intensity Pulses
4 주차: Interaction of Light and Matter: Electron Dynamics vs. Lattice Dynamics
5 주차: Time-Resolved Spectroscopy Techniques (TA, TRPL, 2D-Electronic Spectroscopy)
6 주차: Carrier Generation and Recombination in Semiconductors
7 주차: Hot-Carrier Dynamics and Energy Relaxation Pathways
8 주차: Ultrafast Phase Transitions and Melting
9 주차: Coherent Control of Quantum States
10 주차: Surface and Interface Dynamics in Heterostructures
11 주차: Terahertz Spectroscopy for Carrier Mobility Analysis
12 주차: Applications in Next-Generation Photodetectors and Solar Cells
13 주차: Case Studies in Ultrafast Imaging of Nanodevices
14 주차: Emerging Topics: Attosecond Science and Quantum Information Processing
15 주차: Final Project Presentations and Course Review

detail.query: 유기합성, 촉매개발, 비대칭 합성, 라디칼 반응에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
유기합성개론 (ORG401-01)
교과개요
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the principles and strategies of modern organic synthesis, with a specific focus on catalytic methodologies and asymmetric transformations. Utilizing radical chemistry as a versatile tool for constructing complex molecular architectures, the course explores how transition metal catalysts and organocatalysts can be designed to achieve high enantioselectivity. Students will examine the mechanistic underpinnings of key reactions, learn to predict stereochemical outcomes, and understand how to integrate these advanced techniques into efficient synthetic routes for natural products and pharmaceutical intermediates.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design synthetic pathways that incorporate asymmetric catalysis and radical processes to construct chiral centers with high fidelity. The course aims to equip students with the ability to evaluate catalyst performance, optimize reaction conditions for specific substrates, and communicate complex mechanistic rationales clearly. Furthermore, students will develop a critical perspective on sustainability in synthesis by prioritizing atom economy and catalytic efficiency over stoichiometric reagents.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 현대 유기합성의 패러다임 변화와 촉매의 역할 (Stoichiometric vs. Catalytic)
2 주차: 라디칼 반응의 기초: 생성, 소멸 및 안정성 (Radical Generation and Stability)
3 주차: 금속 촉매를 이용한 라디칼 첨가 반응 메커니즘 (Metal-Catalyzed Radical Addition)
4 주차: 비대칭 합성의 원리: 키랄 보조제와 키랄 리간드 (Principles of Asymmetric Synthesis)
5 주차: 전이금속 촉매를 활용한 라디칼-극성 친핵체 교차 결합 반응 (Cross-Coupling via Radical Intermediates)
6 주차: 유기촉매 (Organocatalysis) 와 라디칼 과정의 시너지 효과 (Synergy between Organocatalysis and Radicals)
7 주차: 촉매 설계 전략: 리간드 조절을 통한 입체선택성 최적화 (Ligand Tuning for Stereoselectivity)
8 주차: 실제 사례 연구: 천연물 합성에서의 라디칼 및 비대칭 촉매 활용 (Case Studies in Natural Product Synthesis)

detail.query: 소재화학, 초분자화학, 대기물수확 소재, 금속유기구조체, 전도성물질에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
소재화학개론 (MAT410-01)
교과개요
This course explores the fundamental principles governing the design and synthesis of advanced materials with tailored properties. We focus on the intersection of chemistry, physics, and engineering to understand how atomic and molecular structures dictate macroscopic behaviors such as conductivity, magnetism, and mechanical strength. Special emphasis is placed on emerging fields including metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for gas harvesting, conductive polymers, and supramolecular assemblies that mimic biological functions. The curriculum bridges theoretical concepts with practical applications in energy storage, environmental remediation, and next-generation electronics.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze structure-property relationships in diverse material systems, design novel materials using principles of coordination chemistry and self-assembly, and evaluate the potential of porous materials like MOFs for carbon capture and water harvesting. Students will also develop skills to interpret spectroscopic data relevant to characterizing conductive and functional materials.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 재료과학의 개요 및 소재화학의 최신 동향 (Introduction to Materials Chemistry & Recent Trends)
2 주차: 원자 간 결합과 전자 구조 (Atomic Bonding and Electronic Structure)
3 주차: 금속유기구조체 (MOFs) 의 합성 및 기공 제어 (Synthesis and Porosity Control of MOFs)
4 주차: 대기 중 이산화탄소 및 수분 포획을 위한 소재 설계 (Design for CO2 and Water Harvesting from Atmosphere)
5 주차: 초분자 화학과 자기조립 시스템 (Supramolecular Chemistry and Self-Assembly Systems)
6 주차: 전도성 고분자와 유기 반도체의 원리 (Principles of Conductive Polymers and Organic Semiconductors)
7 주차: 나노입자 및 양자점의 광학적, 전기적 특성 (Optical and Electrical Properties of Nanoparticles and Quantum Dots)
8 주차: 에너지 저장 소재 (배터리 및 슈퍼커패시터) (Energy Storage Materials for Batteries and Supercapacitors)
9 주차: 촉매로서의 기능성 소재와 지속 가능성 (Functional Materials as Catalysts and Sustainability)
10 주차: 소재의 표면 개질과 계면 공학 (Surface Modification and Interface Engineering of Materials)
11 주차: 생체모방 소재 및 초분자 센서 (Biomimetic Materials and Supramolecular Sensors)
12 주차: 미래 소재 기술의 전망 및 윤리적 고려사항 (Future Perspectives and Ethical Considerations in Material Science)

detail.lab: 비대칭 유기합성 및 의약품 합성 연구실
detail.query: 비대칭 유기합성, 천연물 및 의약품 합성에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
비대칭 유기합성 (ORG450-01)
교과개요
This course explores advanced strategies for constructing complex molecular architectures with high stereochemical precision. Focusing on the synthesis of natural products and pharmaceutical agents, we delve into modern catalytic methodologies including organocatalysis, transition-metal catalysis, and photoredox chemistry. The curriculum bridges fundamental mechanistic understanding with practical synthetic planning, emphasizing how to control chirality at multiple centers during multi-step sequences. Students will analyze classic total syntheses of bioactive molecules and evaluate the efficiency and sustainability of emerging reaction protocols.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design retrosynthetic pathways for chiral targets utilizing asymmetric induction principles, select appropriate catalytic systems for specific bond formations, and predict stereochemical outcomes based on mechanistic models. The course also aims to cultivate critical thinking regarding scalability, atom economy, and the translation of academic synthetic methods into industrial drug discovery contexts.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 입문 - 비대칭 합성의 역사와 중요성 (자연물 구조 분석 사례)
2 주차: 키랄 보조제 기반의 고전적 비대칭 반응 (Sharpless 에폭시화 등)
3 주차: 금속 촉매를 이용한 비대칭 첨가 반응 (알켄 수소화, 알데하이드 알킬화)
4 주차: 유기금속 촉매와 리간드 설계의 원리 (Noyori 환원, Tsuji-Trost 반응)
5 주차: 광촉매 및 전기화학 기반의 새로운 비대칭 합성법
6 주차: 오르가노촉매의 부상 - 프롤린 유도체 및 다른 아민 촉매 활용
7 주차: C-H 활성화와 선택적 기능화 전략 (Pd/Cu 촉매 시스템)
8 주차: 다중 중심 키랄성 제어 - 축합반응과 고리화 반응에서의 입체선택성
9 주차: 천연물 합성 사례 연구 I - 테르펜계 화합물의 총합성 접근법
10 주차: 천연물 합성 사례 연구 II - 알칼로이드 및 페놀성 화합물의 키랄 중심 구축
11 주차: 의약품 개발 관점에서의 비대칭 합성 (API 생산 공정 최적화)
12 주차: 지속 가능한 화학과 비대칭 촉매의 미래 전망 (녹색화학 원칙 적용)

detail.query: 자연모사 유기/고분자 소재, 조직 접착성 하이드로젤, 생체친화적 표면 개질, 간편 분자 진단에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
생체유연소재 및 스마트 진단공학 (BME450-01)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of biomimetic design and advanced polymer science to develop next-generation biomedical materials. We will investigate how natural biological systems achieve superior adhesion, self-healing, and environmental adaptability, translating these principles into synthetic hydrogels and surface modification strategies. The curriculum bridges organic synthesis with tissue engineering applications, focusing on creating bio-compatible interfaces that mimic the extracellular matrix while enabling rapid molecular detection for point-of-care diagnostics.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design biomimetic polymer architectures that replicate specific biological functions such as wet adhesion and enzymatic activity. Students will master surface engineering techniques to enhance cell compatibility and biointegration, formulate hydrogel networks with tunable mechanical properties for soft tissue repair, and develop simplified molecular diagnostic platforms utilizing functionalized nanomaterials.
주차별 강의계획
Week 1: Introduction to Biomimetics and the Principles of Nature-Inspired Materials
Week 2: Fundamentals of Polymer Chemistry and Hydrogel Network Formation
Week 3: Mechanisms of Biological Adhesion (Mussels, Geckos) and Synthetic Mimicry
Week 4: Designing Tissue-Adhesive Hydrogels for Soft Tissue Repair Applications
Week 5: Surface Modification Strategies for Bio-compatibility and Anti-fouling Properties
Week 6: Functionalizing Surfaces with Biomolecules (Peptides, Proteins, DNA)
Week 7: Smart Materials: Stimuli-Responsive Polymers in Drug Delivery Systems
Week 8: Midterm Examination and Project Proposal Presentation
Week 9: Principles of Molecular Diagnostics and Biosensor Design
Week 10: Enzyme-Mediated Signal Amplification for Rapid Detection Assays
Week 11: Fabrication of Paper-Based Microfluidic Devices for Point-of-Care Testing
Week 12: Integration of Hydrogel Matrices with Diagnostic Sensors
Week 13: Case Studies in Clinical Translation of Biomimetic Materials
Week 14: Group Project Presentations and Final Review

detail.query: 제일원리, 머신러닝에 기반한 양자물성연구/통계물리에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
양자정보와 머신러닝 (PHY5XX-01)
교과개요
This course explores the emerging intersection of quantum mechanics, statistical physics, and machine learning. We will investigate how neural networks can be used to solve complex many-body problems in condensed matter physics, such as finding ground states of interacting spin systems or simulating quantum dynamics. The curriculum bridges the gap between theoretical foundations of quantum information (entanglement, density matrices) and practical applications of deep learning architectures (variational autoencoders, generative models) to analyze phase transitions and critical phenomena.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to formulate statistical mechanical problems using machine learning frameworks, implement variational quantum eigensolvers for simple lattice models, and interpret high-dimensional data from quantum simulations to identify topological order or symmetry breaking patterns. The course aims to equip students with the interdisciplinary skills necessary to lead research at the frontier of quantum materials discovery and AI-driven physics.
주차별 강의계획
Week 1: Introduction to Quantum Machine Learning - Basics of Neural Networks for Physics
Week 2: Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) vs. Deep Learning Approaches
Week 3: Variational Autoencoders (VAE) for Phase Classification in Spin Systems
Week 4: Generative Models for Quantum State Tomography and Simulation
Week 5: Symmetry-Protected Topological Phases and Neural Network Representations
Week 6: Reinforcement Learning for Controlling Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
Week 7: Midterm Project Presentation - Applying ML to a Specific Hamiltonian Model
Week 8: Diffusion Models for Generating Realistic Atomic Structures in Materials Science
Week 9: Transfer Learning from Classical Statistical Physics to Quantum Regimes
Week 10: Quantum Circuit Learning and Hybrid Classical-Quantum Algorithms
Week 11: Analysis of Large-Scale Simulation Data using Unsupervised Learning
Week 12: Ethics and Future Directions in AI for Fundamental Physics Research
Week 13: Group Project Workshop - Designing a Novel ML Architecture for Many-Body Problems
Week 14: Final Project Presentations and Critical Review
Week 15: Course Summary and Open Discussion on Frontiers of Quantum-AI Synergy

detail.query: 초전도 회로 기반 양자 전산과 센싱에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
양자회로 및 양자센싱 (PHY501-01)
교과개요
This course explores the principles and applications of superconducting circuits in quantum computing and sensing. Utilizing Josephson junctions as nonlinear inductors, we will examine how macroscopic quantum phenomena are engineered into scalable qubit architectures such as transmon and fluxonium. The curriculum bridges condensed matter physics with circuit theory to address decoherence mechanisms, control protocols, and readout strategies. Special attention is given to the design of high-sensitivity magnetometers and electrometers that leverage quantum non-demolition measurements for nanoscale sensing applications.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to model superconducting circuit Hamiltonians, design pulse sequences for quantum gate operations, and analyze noise spectra in qubit systems. The course aims to equip students with the skills to propose novel architectures for fault-tolerant quantum processors and develop sensitive detection schemes for fundamental physics experiments using superconducting devices.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 양자 회로 물리학의 기초 및 조셉슨 접합 (Josephson Junction) 동역학
2 주차: 초전도 큐비트 아키텍처 (Transmon, Fluxonium 등) 및 에너지 준위 구조
3 주차: 양자 게이트 연산 및 펄스 제어 이론 (Microwave Control)
4 주차: 결맞음 시간 (Coherence Time) 제한 요인 및 노이즈 스펙트럼 분석
5 주차: 양자 오류 정정 코드 및 논리 큐비트 구현 전략
6 주차: 초전도 기반 양자 센서 원리 (SQUID, Dispersive Readout)
7 주차: 양자 비파괴 측정 (Quantum Non-Demolition Measurement) 기술
8 주차: 나노 스케일 자기장 및 전기장 감지 응용 사례 연구
9 주차: 2D 물질 및 초전도 이종접합을 활용한 하이브리드 양자 시스템
10 주차: 양자 회로 시뮬레이션 툴킷 활용 및 실험 설계 프로젝트 발표

detail.query: 초고속 동역학, 적외선 분광학, 강상관계 양자물질에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
초고속 동역학 및 강상관계 물질 (PHY495-01)
교과개요
This course explores the ultrafast dynamics of strongly correlated quantum materials using advanced spectroscopic techniques, with a specific focus on time-resolved infrared (TRIR) and terahertz spectroscopy. We will investigate how electron-electron interactions, lattice distortions, and charge ordering evolve on femtosecond to picosecond timescales following photo-excitation. The curriculum bridges the gap between condensed matter theory and experimental observation, enabling students to interpret complex spectral signatures in materials such as transition metal oxides, high-temperature superconductors, and topological insulators.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design experiments utilizing ultrafast laser pulses to probe non-equilibrium states in quantum matter, analyze time-domain spectroscopic data to extract relaxation timescales and coupling strengths, and critically evaluate theoretical models describing strong correlation effects under dynamic conditions. The course also aims to foster an understanding of how light-matter interactions can induce novel phases or control material properties on ultrafast timescales.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 강상관계 물질의 기초 및 초고속 분광학 원리 (강상관계 현상, 광 여기 메커니즘)
2 주차: 시간 분해 적외선 분광법 (TRIR) 의 이론적 배경 및 실험 구성
3 주차: 전하 밀도 파동 (CDW) 및 스핀 밀도 파동 (SDW) 의 초고속 동역학
4 주차: 격자-전자 결합 (Electron-Phonon Coupling) 분석을 위한 적외선 흡수 스펙트럼 해석
5 주차: 강상관계 절연체에서의 광유도 금속성 전이 및 비평형 상태 역학
6 주차: 고온 초전도체의 쿠퍼 쌍 형성 및 파괴 과정의 시간 분해 관측
7 주차: 위상 절연체 및 스카이미온 동역학의 적외선 신호 탐지
8 주차: 테라헤르츠 분광학을 이용한 저에너지 여기 모드 연구
9 주차: 데이터 분석 실습 (스펙트럼 피팅, 상관관계 함수 계산)
10 주차: 강상관계 시스템에서의 열화 과정 및 에너지 재분배 메커니즘
11 주차: 최근 연구 동향 및 차세대 초고속 분광 기술 (X-ray pump-probe 등)
12 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 최종 평가

detail.query: Strongly Correlated Systems, Quantum Many-Body Physics, Quantum Monte Carlo Method에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
양자 다체 물리 및 몬테카를로 시뮬레이션 (PHY5XX-01)
교과개요
This course explores the theoretical and computational methods required to understand strongly correlated quantum systems, where mean-field approximations fail. We focus on Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) techniques as a primary tool for solving many-body problems without sign-problem limitations or by addressing them via advanced algorithms. The curriculum bridges condensed matter theory, statistical mechanics, and high-performance computing, enabling students to simulate complex materials such as high-temperature superconductors, quantum magnets, and topological phases from first principles.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to formulate many-body Hamiltonians for interacting fermion and boson systems, implement stochastic sampling algorithms (e.g., Diffusion Monte Carlo, Auxiliary Field QMC) to calculate ground-state energies and correlation functions, and critically analyze numerical results in the context of phase transitions and emergent phenomena. The course also aims to develop proficiency in writing efficient C++/Python codes for large-scale parallel simulations on supercomputers.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 강상관 양자 다체계의 물리적 배경 및 평균장 이론의 한계 (Hubbard Model 소개)
2~3 주차: 양자 몬테카를로 (QMC) 방법론의 기초 - 경로 적분 표현과 확률적 해석
4~5 주차: 확산 몬테카를로 (DMC) 알고리즘 구현 및 바닥상태 에너지 계산 원리
6~7 주차: 보조장 QMC (AFQMC) 와 페르미온 시그널 문제 해결 전략
8~9 주차: 양자 자기체 및 스핀 액체 상태의 QMC 시뮬레이션 사례 연구
10~11 주차: 고온 초전도체 모델에서의 위상학적 상전이 분석 및 데이터 해석
12~13 주차: 대규모 병렬 컴퓨팅 환경에서의 QMC 코드 최적화 및 실습
14 주차: 최신 연구 동향 (Tensor Network 등) 과 종합 프로젝트 발표

detail.query: Quantum Transport, Quantum Engineering & Computing에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
양자 수송 및 양자 공학 개론 (PHY410-01)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of condensed matter physics and quantum information science, focusing on how quantum coherence and entanglement manifest in mesoscopic systems. We will investigate electron transport through nanostructures, quantum Hall effects, and topological phases of matter. The curriculum bridges theoretical frameworks like non-equilibrium Green's functions with practical engineering challenges in designing scalable quantum devices. Students will analyze the role of decoherence in quantum circuits and examine recent breakthroughs in superconducting qubits and spin-based architectures.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to model quantum transport phenomena using scattering theory and density matrix formalism, design basic protocols for initializing and manipulating qubits, and evaluate trade-offs between coherence time and device scalability. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to translate fundamental quantum mechanical principles into viable engineering solutions for next-generation computing platforms.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 양자 수송의 기초와 메조스코픽 물리 (Mesoscopic Physics)
2 주차: 산란 이론과 전도도 계산 (Scattering Theory and Conductance)
3 주차: 비평형 그린 함수 (Non-equilibrium Green's Functions) 소개
4 주차: 양자 홀 효과 및 위상 절연체 (Quantum Hall Effect & Topological Insulators)
5 주차: 결맞음 (Coherence) 과 얽힘 (Entanglement) 의 물리적 구현
6 주차: 초전도 큐비트와 조셉슨 접합 공학 (Superconducting Qubits and Josephson Junctions)
7 주차: 스핀 기반 양자 컴퓨팅 및 자기공명 (Spin-based Quantum Computing & NMR)
8 주차: 양자 오류 정정 코드와 논리 큐비트 설계 (Quantum Error Correction Codes)
9 주차: 양자 센싱과 나노구조체에서의 측정 문제 (Quantum Sensing in Nanostructures)
10 주차: 하이브리드 양자 시스템 및 인터페이스 공학 (Hybrid Quantum Systems & Interfaces)
11 주차: 양자 알고리즘의 하드웨어 제약 조건 분석 (Hardware Constraints for Quantum Algorithms)
12 주차: 최신 연구 동향과 양자 기술의 상용화 전망 (Recent Advances and Commercialization Prospects)

detail.query: 초전도체, 자성체, 위상물질, 단결정합성, 저온물리특성, Xray와 중성자산란에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
초전도 및 응집물질물리학개론 (PHY415-01)
교과개요
This course explores the quantum mechanical phenomena arising in condensed matter systems, with a specific focus on superconductivity, magnetism, and topological phases. Utilizing concepts from many-body physics and statistical mechanics, we will investigate how macroscopic properties emerge from microscopic interactions. The curriculum bridges theoretical frameworks with experimental techniques, covering single-crystal growth methods, low-temperature characterization, and scattering experiments using X-rays and neutrons to probe electronic and magnetic structures.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to derive key equations describing superconducting transitions and magnetic ordering, analyze topological invariants in band structures, and interpret data from diffraction and spectroscopy experiments. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of how material synthesis influences physical properties and enables the design of next-generation quantum materials.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 응집물질물리학의 기초와 페르미 액체 이론
2 주차: 초전도 현상의 역사적 발견과 BCS 이론 개론
3 주차: Ginzburg-Landau 이론과 자발적 대칭성 깨짐
4 주차: 강자성체, 반강자성체 및 스핀파 동역학
5 주차: 위상 절연체와 베리 곡률의 물리적 의미
6 주차: 위상 초전도체와 마요라나 페르미온
7 주차: 단결정 성장 기술 (브로크, Czochralski 법) 과 결함 제어
8 주차: 저온 물리 실험 기법 (희석 냉각기 및 열량계 원리)
9 주차: X-ray 회절 (XRD) 을 통한 결정 구조 분석과 전자 밀도 분포
10 주차: 중성자 산란을 이용한 자기 구조와 스핀 동역학 연구
11 주차: 초전도체의 위상 전이와 임계 매개변수 측정
12 주차: 위상 물질의 표면 상태와 양자 홀 효과
13 주차: 실험 데이터 해석 사례 연구 (산란 패턴 및 전기적 특성)
14 주차: 차세대 양자 컴퓨팅을 위한 물질 탐색 전략
15 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 최종 평가

detail.query: 양자물질, 저차원 물질, 양자현미경(STM)에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
양자저차원물리 (PHY501-01)
교과개요
This course explores the unique physical phenomena arising in low-dimensional systems such as 2D materials, nanowires, and quantum wells. Utilizing Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) and related spectroscopic techniques as a central theme, we bridge the gap between theoretical models of electron confinement and experimental observations of electronic structure. Students will investigate topological phases, fractional quantum Hall effects, and emergent collective excitations in strongly correlated systems, with a specific focus on interpreting STM data to map local density of states and atomic-scale electronic structures.
교과목표
By the end of the semester, students should be able to derive analytical solutions for Schrödinger equations in reduced dimensions, apply many-body perturbation theory to understand electron-phonon coupling, and critically analyze experimental STM images and dI/dV spectra to extract information about surface states, defect structures, and quantum confinement effects. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to design experiments that probe quantum coherence and transport properties in novel materials.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: Introduction to Low-Dimensional Physics & Quantum Confinement
2 주차: Tight-Binding Model in 1D and 2D Lattices
3 주차: Density of States in Zero, One, and Two Dimensions
4 주차: Electronic Structure of Graphene and Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs)
5 주차: Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) Principles and Theory
6 주차: STM Imaging Techniques: Constant Current vs. Constant Height Modes
7 주차: Analysis of Local Density of States (LDOS) via dI/dV Spectroscopy
8 주차: Surface States and Fermi Level Pinning in 2D Materials
9 주차: Quantum Hall Effect and Topological Insulators
10 주차: Fractional Quantum Hall Effect and Composite Fermions
11 주차: Electron-Phonon Coupling and Polaron Formation
12 주차: STM Studies of Superconductivity and Majorana Modes
13 주차: Correlated Electron Systems in Low Dimensions
14 주차: Advanced Topics: Moiré Patterns and Twistronics
15 주차: Experimental Design for Quantum Material Characterization
16 주차: Final Project Presentations and Course Review

detail.query: 나노 스핀 소자, 응집물질 물리, 자성체 및 자성 박막에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
나노스핀물리학개론 (PHY501-01)
교과개요
This course explores the fundamental principles governing magnetic phenomena at the nanoscale, bridging the gap between bulk magnetism and device physics. We will examine how dimensionality reduction alters electronic structure, spin dynamics, and magnetic ordering in low-dimensional systems such as 2D materials, quantum wells, and nanostructures. The curriculum integrates concepts from condensed matter theory, including band theory, density functional theory basics, and spin transport mechanisms (e.g., Giant Magnetoresistance, Tunneling Magnetoresistance). Special attention is paid to the interface physics of magnetic heterostructures, domain wall dynamics, and the manipulation of spin states using electric fields or spin-orbit torque.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze the relationship between material properties (crystal structure, anisotropy) and macroscopic magnetic behaviors in nano-devices. Students will master the theoretical frameworks describing spin injection, detection, and manipulation, enabling them to design simple spintronic concepts. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of how quantum mechanical effects manifest in magnetic thin films and nanodevices, preparing students for advanced research in spintronics and next-generation memory technologies.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 나노스핀 소자의 물리적 배경 및 개요 (Bulk vs. Nano magnetism)
2 주차: 응집물질 물리학 기초: 밴드 이론과 전자 구조
3 주차: 자성체의 미시적 기원: 교환 상호작용과 자기 정렬
4 주차: 저차원 시스템에서의 자기 현상: 양자 우물과 2D 물질의 자성
5 주차: 스핀 전수송 현상: GMR 및 TMR 원리 이해
6 주차: 자성 박막의 계면 물리 및 합금 효과
7 주차: 도메인 벽 역학 및 나노선에서의 자기적 성질
8 주차: 스핀 - 오비트 결합 (SOC) 과 전기장 제어 가능성
9 주차: 스핀 주입 및 검출 메커니즘 (Spin Injection/Detection)
10 주차: 자성 메모리 소자 구조 및 동작 원리 (MRAM 등)
11 주차: 최신 연구 동향: 토크 기반 스위칭 및 논리 소자
12 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 미래 전망

detail.query: 고체물리이론, 초고속동역학, 비평형현상, 제일원리계산에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
고체물리이론, 초고속동역학, 비평형현상, 제일원리계산을 아우르는 통합적인 접근을 가능하게 하는 가상의 강의계획서입니다.

고체물리 및 비평형계산 (PHY450-01)
교과개요
This course explores the theoretical foundations of condensed matter physics with a specific focus on non-equilibrium dynamics and ultrafast phenomena. Utilizing first-principles computational methods, we bridge the gap between static electronic structure calculations and time-dependent response functions. The curriculum covers density functional theory (DFT) extensions for excited states, many-body perturbation theory, and molecular dynamics simulations to analyze how materials evolve under extreme conditions or intense laser fields. Students will learn to model phase transitions, carrier relaxation processes, and topological properties in both equilibrium and driven systems.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate Hamiltonians for interacting many-body systems, apply computational techniques to predict material properties under non-equilibrium conditions, and interpret ultrafast spectroscopic data through theoretical frameworks. The course aims to equip students with the skills to design novel materials for optoelectronics and quantum technologies by understanding the interplay between electronic structure and dynamic evolution.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 고체물리 이론의 현대적 관점과 비평형 통계역학 기초
2 주차: 제일원리 계산 (DFT) 의 기본 원리와 전자 구조 해석
3 주차: 밀도범함수이론 (DFT) 을 넘어선 여기 상태와 다체 섭동론 소개
4 주차: 초고속 동역학의 물리적 배경과 펨토초 레이저 - 물질 상호작용
5 주차: 비평형 그린 함수 formalism 과 시간 의존 슈뢰딩거 방정식 수치해법
6 주차: 전하 및 에너지 이송 과정 모델링 (Drude 모델 및 그 이상)
7 주차: 분자동역학 (MD) 시뮬레이션과 열적화 과정 분석
8 주차: 위상 물질의 비평형 동역학과 양자 정보 전달 메커니즘
9 주차: 강상관 전자계에서의 초고속 상전이 현상 연구
10 주차: 실제 실험 데이터와 이론 계산 결과 비교 및 종합 프로젝트 발표

detail.query: 반도체, 포토닉스 정보소자, 빛-물질 상호작용에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
반도체 및 나노광전자공학개론 (PHY450-01)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of semiconductor physics and photonics, focusing on how light interacts with matter at the nanoscale. We will examine the fundamental principles governing optoelectronic devices, including LEDs, lasers, photodetectors, and solar cells. The curriculum bridges the gap between bulk material properties and device-level performance, emphasizing the manipulation of electron-hole pairs through optical excitation and electrical injection. Special attention is given to emerging topics such as plasmonics, metamaterials, and integrated photonic circuits for information processing.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze the band structure engineering required for efficient light emission and detection, design basic optoelectronic devices using semiconductor heterostructures, and evaluate the trade-offs between optical confinement, carrier recombination rates, and thermal management. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of light-matter interaction mechanisms essential for developing next-generation information elements and photonic integrated systems.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 반도체 물성 및 밴드 구조 기초 (Band Structure & Density of States)
2 주차: 광흡수 및 광발생 과정 (Absorption, Emission, and Recombination Dynamics)
3 주차: p-n 접합과 다이오드의 광학적 특성 (Optical Properties of p-n Junctions)
4 주차: 레이저 물리 및 반도체 레이저 원리 (Semiconductor Lasers & Population Inversion)
5 주차: 광검출기 및 포토다이오드 동작 원리 (Photodetectors and Responsivity)
6 주차: 태양전지 효율 극대화 전략 (Solar Cell Efficiency Limits & Passivation)
7 주차: 플라즈모닉스 및 표면 등방성 진공 방출 (Plasmonics & Surface-Enhanced Phenomena)
8 주차: 메타물질과 인공 구조물을 이용한 빛 제어 (Metamaterials and Light Control)
9 주차: 포토닉 크리스탈 및 광결정 공학 (Photonic Crystals and Bandgap Engineering)
10 주차: 실리콘 포토닉스 및 집적 광회로 설계 기초 (Silicon Photonics & PIC Design Basics)
11 주차: 빛-물질 강결합 및 캐비티 Q 인자 최적화 (Strong Coupling & Cavity Q-Factor Optimization)
12 주차: 양자점 및 2D 물질 기반 나노광전자 소자 (Nanoscale Optoelectronics with Quantum Dots & 2D Materials)
13 주차: 광소자의 열적 안정성 및 신뢰성 평가 (Thermal Stability and Reliability of Optical Devices)
14 주차: 최신 연구 동향 및 미래 정보소자 전망 (Future Trends in Photonic Information Elements)

detail.lab: 극저온 원자 및 양자 시스템 설계 연구실
detail.query: 극저온 원자 기반 양자 시뮬레이션 및 양자 컴퓨터에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
양자 다체 물리 및 시뮬레이션 (PHY5XX-01)
교과개요
This course explores the application of ultracold atomic gases and trapped ions as programmable quantum simulators to investigate many-body physics that is intractable for classical computers. Utilizing concepts from quantum optics, condensed matter theory, and control engineering, students will learn how to engineer Hamiltonians with cold atoms to model complex phenomena such as high-temperature superconductivity, topological phases of matter, and non-equilibrium dynamics. The curriculum bridges the gap between abstract quantum field theories and experimental realizations in optical lattices and tweezer arrays, emphasizing the design of quantum circuits for error mitigation and readout strategies.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate effective Hamiltonians for cold atom systems, analyze phase transitions in quantum simulators using tensor network methods, and design basic quantum algorithms for simulation tasks. The course also aims to equip students with the skills to interpret experimental data from quantum platforms and communicate the potential of hybrid classical-quantum approaches for solving complex many-body problems.

---

양자 알고리즘 및 하드웨어 (CS5XX-01)
교과개요
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the architecture of quantum computers and the development of algorithms tailored for near-term devices (NISQ). Topics include qubit physics, gate-based operations, error correction codes, and variational quantum eigensolvers (VQE). Students will study how to map combinatorial optimization problems and quantum chemistry simulations onto quantum hardware, focusing on noise-resilient techniques. The course integrates theoretical computer science with practical considerations of coherence times and gate fidelities, preparing students to write and optimize quantum programs for platforms like superconducting circuits and trapped ions.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to construct quantum circuits for specific simulation tasks, apply error mitigation strategies to improve result fidelity, and evaluate the scalability of quantum algorithms for scientific computing. The course also aims to strengthen the ability to translate physical problems into qubit representations and clearly articulate the limitations and advantages of current quantum hardware in research contexts.

detail.query: 나노물질의 전기적/자기적 성징에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
나노전자물리개론 (PHY450-01)
교과개요
This course explores the unique electrical and magnetic properties emerging when materials are confined to the nanoscale. Utilizing concepts from condensed matter physics and quantum mechanics, we investigate how size reduction alters band structures, density of states, and spin dynamics. The curriculum bridges fundamental theory with cutting-edge applications in spintronics, quantum computing, and next-generation sensors. Students will analyze phenomena such as quantum confinement, giant magnetoresistance, and single-electron transport to understand the design principles of nanodevices.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to predict how dimensional changes affect electronic and magnetic behaviors in various nanostructures. The course aims to equip students with the tools to interpret experimental data from scanning probe microscopy and transport measurements, formulate hypotheses for novel nanomaterial synthesis, and communicate the physical mechanisms underlying emerging nanoelectronic technologies clearly.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 나노물리학의 기초와 양자 구속 효과 (Quantum Confinement)
2 주차: 나노입자의 전자구조와 밴드갭 조절 (Band Gap Engineering)
3 주차: 나노선 및 양자점에서의 전하 수송 현상 (Charge Transport in Nanowires and Quantum Dots)
4 주차: 자성 나노입자와 초상자성 (Superparamagnetism)
5 주차: 거대자기저항 (GMR) 과 스핀트로닉스 기초
6 주차: 단일 전자 트랜지스터 및 쿨롱 봉쇄 효과 (Coulomb Blockade)
7 주차: 나노물질의 자기 공명 특성 및 스핀 조작
8 주차: 나노구조를 이용한 양자 정보 처리 소자
9 주차: 2 차원 물질 (그래핀 등) 의 전기적 성질과 디랙 페르미온
10 주차: 나노자기소자의 응용: 고밀도 저장 매체 및 센서
11 주차: 나노복합재료의 다기능성 (전기/자기 결합 현상)
12 주차: 최신 연구 동향과 미래 전망 (Post-Silicon Nanoelectronics)

detail.query: 반도체, 에너지, 센서, 박막, 나노구조에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
반도체 및 나노소자물리 (PHY415-01)
교과개요
This course explores the fundamental physics governing semiconductor devices and nanostructured materials, with a specific focus on energy conversion and sensing applications. Utilizing concepts from solid-state physics and quantum mechanics, we examine carrier transport mechanisms, band structure engineering, and interface phenomena in thin films. The curriculum bridges theoretical models with practical device architectures used in photovoltaics, thermoelectrics, and high-sensitivity sensors. Students will analyze how nanoscale confinement alters electronic properties and learn to design materials for optimized energy efficiency and detection limits.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to derive key transport equations for semiconductors, interpret experimental data from thin-film characterization techniques, and evaluate trade-offs between material properties and device performance in energy and sensing applications. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to propose novel nanostructure designs that enhance carrier mobility or quantum efficiency for next-generation electronic and optoelectronic systems.

---

나노박막 공정 및 물성 (MAT420-01)
교과개요
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the synthesis, processing, and physical properties of thin films and nanostructures relevant to semiconductor and energy technologies. Topics include physical vapor deposition (PVD), chemical vapor deposition (CVD), sputtering, and atomic layer deposition (ALD), along with their impact on film morphology, crystallinity, and defect density. We investigate how microstructure influences electrical conductivity, optical absorption, and mechanical stability in sensor and solar cell applications. The course integrates hands-on analysis of structure-property relationships to guide the development of functional materials for specific device requirements.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to select appropriate deposition techniques for target material systems, correlate processing parameters with resulting film quality, and predict how nanostructural features affect macroscopic device performance. The course also aims to strengthen skills in interpreting advanced characterization data (e.g., XRD, AFM, SEM) and communicating technical findings regarding energy harvesting or sensing mechanisms effectively.

detail.query: Human-Computer Interaction(HCI) / VR/AR/MR Interaction / Text Entry, / Multi-sensory Haptics / Wearable & Smart Glasses Interfaces에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
HCI 및 몰입형 인터페이스 (VR/AR), 텍스트 입력, 다감각 햅틱스, 웨어러블 디바이스 인터페이스 분야를 심층적으로 다루는 가상의 강의계획서입니다. 요청하신 형식에 맞춰 행정 정보는 모두 제외하고 본문만 출력합니다.

Human-Computer Interaction for Immersive Environments (HCI4IM)
교과개요
This course explores the design, evaluation, and implementation of interactive systems within immersive environments such as Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), and Mixed Reality (MR). We move beyond traditional desktop paradigms to address unique challenges in spatial computing, including 3D user interfaces, gaze-based interaction, and seamless integration of digital content with the physical world. Special attention is given to text entry methods optimized for head-mounted displays, multi-sensory haptic feedback mechanisms, and ergonomic considerations for wearable smart glasses. The curriculum bridges theoretical frameworks of human perception with practical prototyping using modern XR development kits.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design intuitive interaction models tailored to immersive contexts, develop custom input methods for constrained environments like VR headsets or AR glasses, and integrate multi-modal feedback (visual, auditory, haptic) to enhance user experience. Students will gain proficiency in evaluating spatial usability and comfort, ultimately creating prototypes that effectively leverage wearable technologies for novel computing experiences.

주차별 강의계획
Week 1: Introduction to Immersive Computing - From Desktop to Spatial Interfaces
Week 2: Human Factors in XR - Perception, Cognition, and Ergonomics for Wearables
Week 3: Interaction Design Principles for VR/AR/MR Environments
Week 4: Text Entry in Immersive Spaces - Challenges and Solutions (Gaze, Gesture, Voice)
Week 5: Multi-Sensory Haptics - Force Feedback, Tactile Gloves, and Smart Fabric Integration
Week 6: Wearable & Smart Glasses Interfaces - Form Factors, Display Technologies, and User Comfort
Week 7: Eye-Tracking and Gaze-Based Interaction Systems
Week 8: Midterm Project Proposal - Defining an Immersive Interaction Problem
Week 9: Prototyping with XR Development Kits (Unity/Unreal/OpenXR)
Week 10: Multi-Modal Feedback Integration - Synchronizing Visual, Auditory, and Haptic Cues
Week 11: User Evaluation Methods for Spatial Interfaces - Metrics beyond Accuracy
Week 12: Case Studies in Commercial VR/AR Products and Future Trends
Week 13: Advanced Topics - Brain-Computer Interfaces and Neural Haptics
Week 14: Final Project Presentation and Peer Review

detail.query: AI Training & Tuning / AI for Software Engineering / Data for AI /, Architecture Design / Model Engineering에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
AI 시스템 아키텍처 및 엔지니어링 (CS590-01)
교과개요
This course bridges the gap between theoretical deep learning and production-grade AI system design. We move beyond standard model training to focus on scalable architecture patterns, efficient data pipelines for fine-tuning, and robust software engineering practices for deploying large models. The curriculum integrates principles of Model Engineering with practical strategies for optimizing inference latency, managing memory constraints, and ensuring reliability in real-world software environments. Students will explore how to architect systems that leverage diverse data sources for continuous learning while maintaining strict quality control over the generated outputs.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design modular AI architectures tailored to specific domain requirements, engineer efficient data workflows for pre-training and tuning phases, and implement rigorous testing protocols for model reliability. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to translate complex research concepts into maintainable software components, enabling students to lead projects that integrate advanced AI capabilities seamlessly into existing engineering stacks.

주차별 강의계획
Week 1: Introduction to AI System Engineering - From Research Prototypes to Production Systems
Week 2: Architectural Patterns for Large Language Models (LLMs) - Modular Design and Service Orchestration
Week 3: Data-Centric AI - Building Robust Pipelines for Pre-training, Fine-tuning, and RAG
Week 4: Model Engineering Fundamentals - Quantization, Pruning, and Knowledge Distillation Strategies
Week 5: Efficient Training at Scale - Distributed Computing, Gradient Accumulation, and Checkpoint Management
Week 6: Tuning Techniques in Practice - LoRA, QLoRA, and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Implementation
Week 7: Software Engineering for AI - Version Control for Models, CI/CD for ML Pipelines, and Testing Frameworks
Week 8: Midterm Project Proposal - Designing an End-to-End AI System Architecture
Week 9: Inference Optimization - Latency Reduction, Caching Strategies, and Hardware-Aware Deployment
Week 10: Safety, Alignment, and Evaluation Metrics - Building Trustworthy and Responsible AI Systems
Week 11: Cross-Disciplinary Integration - Connecting AI Capabilities with Legacy Software Ecosystems
Week 12: Capstone Project Implementation - Building a Scalable Data Pipeline and Model Serving Layer
Week 13: Advanced Architecture Design - Handling Multimodal Inputs and Complex Reasoning Workloads
Week 14: Future Trends in AI Engineering - Agentic Systems, AutoML, and Sustainable AI Practices
Week 15: Final Capstone Project Presentation and Defense

detail.query: Embedded software / Software Verification /, Autonomous systems / Cyber-Physical Systems에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Embedded Systems Security & Formal Verification (CS450)
교과개요
This course bridges the gap between embedded software development and rigorous system verification. We explore how to design autonomous agents and cyber-physical systems that are not only functionally correct but also provably secure against adversarial inputs and hardware faults. Utilizing formal methods, model checking, and static analysis tools, students will learn to mathematically verify safety-critical code before deployment. The curriculum integrates theoretical foundations of temporal logic with practical case studies from autonomous driving, industrial robotics, and IoT networks, emphasizing the transition from heuristic testing to guaranteed correctness.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to model embedded system behaviors using formal specifications, apply automated verification techniques to detect vulnerabilities in control software, and design fault-tolerant architectures for autonomous systems. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to critically evaluate trade-offs between computational efficiency and verification rigor, enabling engineers to build trustworthy cyber-physical infrastructures that adhere to strict safety standards.

주차별 강의계획
Week 1: Introduction to Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Safety-Critical Software
Week 2: Fundamentals of Formal Methods: Propositional and Temporal Logic
Week 3: Model Checking Basics: State Spaces, Reachability Analysis, and LTL Verification
Week 4: Static Analysis for Embedded Code: Data Flow Analysis and Control Flow Graphs
Week 5: Security in Embedded Systems: Side-Channel Attacks and Memory Safety
Week 6: Adversarial Machine Learning in Autonomous Agents
Week 7: Hardware-Software Co-Design for Verifiability
Week 8: Midterm Project Proposal: Designing a Verification Pipeline for a CPS Prototype
Week 9: Symbolic Execution and Constraint Solving (SMT)
Week 10: Runtime Monitoring and Self-Healing Systems
Week 11: Case Study: Formal Verification of Autonomous Driving Controllers
Week 12: Case Study: Secure Firmware Updates in IoT Networks
Week 13: Distributed Consensus and Fault Tolerance in CPS
Week 14: Ethical Implications of Unverifiable AI in Critical Infrastructure
Week 15: Final Project Presentation and Defense

detail.query: Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Human-Computer Interaction Fundamentals (HCI101)
교과개요
This course introduces the core principles and methodologies of designing interactive systems that effectively meet user needs. We explore the intersection of computer science, psychology, and design to understand how humans perceive, process information, and interact with digital interfaces. The curriculum covers usability engineering, user-centered design processes, cognitive load theory, and accessibility standards. Through iterative prototyping and evaluation techniques, students will learn to bridge the gap between technical implementation and human experience, ensuring that technology serves its users intuitively and ethically.

교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to conduct comprehensive user research to define problem spaces, apply established design frameworks to create wireframes and prototypes, and evaluate interface effectiveness using quantitative and qualitative metrics. The course aims to cultivate a mindset that prioritizes empathy for users while maintaining rigorous analytical skills to validate design decisions with data.

주차별 강의계획
Week 1: Introduction to HCI - History, Scope, and the Human-Computer Loop
Week 2: Cognitive Psychology Basics - Perception, Memory, and Attention in Interface Design
Week 3: User-Centered Design Process - Requirements Gathering and Persona Development
Week 4: Information Architecture - Organizing Content for Clarity and Navigation
Week 5: Visual Design Principles - Typography, Color, Layout, and Gestalt Laws
Week 6: Interaction Design Patterns - Common UI Components and Behavioral Expectations
Week 7: Usability Engineering - Heuristics, Evaluation Methods, and Testing Protocols
Week 8: Accessibility and Inclusive Design - Standards (WCAG) and Universal Design Principles
Week 9: Mobile and Touch Interface Design - Gestures, Responsiveness, and Context Awareness
Week 10: Data-Driven Design - A/B Testing, Analytics, and Iterative Improvement
Week 11: Emerging Trends in HCI - Voice Interfaces, AR/VR, and AI-Assisted Interaction
Week 12: Capstone Project Presentation - Critique and Final Defense

detail.query: Formal Verification / Real-Time System Verification / Consensus Algorithms, / Compiler Verification / Programming Languages / Provable AI에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Formal Methods for Reliable Systems (CS590-01)
교과개요
This course explores the mathematical foundations and practical applications of formal verification techniques to ensure correctness in complex software and hardware systems. We will cover model checking, theorem proving, and static analysis methods tailored for real-time systems and distributed consensus algorithms. Special attention is given to verifying compiler transformations, programming language semantics, and emerging challenges in provable AI, where we aim to establish rigorous guarantees for machine learning models and their integration into safety-critical environments.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to construct formal specifications for real-time protocols and consensus mechanisms, apply automated theorem proving tools to verify compiler optimizations and language-level properties, and design verification frameworks that provide mathematical proofs for AI algorithmic stability and security. The course aims to equip students with the skills to bridge theoretical computer science with industrial-grade reliability requirements in next-generation computing systems.

주차별 강의계획
Week 1: Introduction to Formal Verification - Models, Specifications, and Proof Systems
Week 2: Logic Foundations for Hardware and Software Verification (Temporal Logic, Hoare Logic)
Week 3: Model Checking Basics - State Spaces, Reachability Analysis, and LTL/CTL
Week 4: Advanced Model Checking Techniques - Abstraction, Symbolic Execution, and Bounded Model Checking
Week 5: Real-Time System Verification - Timed Automata and UPPAAL Case Studies
Week 6: Distributed Systems and Consensus Algorithms - Formalizing Paxos/Raft and Safety/Liveness Properties
Week 7: Compiler Verification - Verifying Optimizations, Type Preservation, and Memory Models
Week 8: Programming Language Semantics - Operational vs. Denotational Semantics in Verification Contexts
Week 9: Intermediate Logic for AI - Reasoning about Neural Networks and Probabilistic Programs

detail.query: Decision-Making AI, Multimodal AI, Autonomous Systems, (Autonomous driving, robots)에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Decision-Making AI for Autonomous Systems (CS590-01)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of artificial intelligence and autonomous decision-making, focusing on algorithms that enable agents to perceive environments, reason about uncertainties, and execute complex tasks in dynamic settings. We move beyond static pattern recognition to address sequential decision problems under partial observability, integrating concepts from reinforcement learning, probabilistic planning, and control theory. Special attention is given to multimodal data fusion—combining visual, LiDAR, and textual inputs—to build robust perception systems for autonomous driving and robotic manipulation. The curriculum emphasizes safety-critical applications, ethical constraints in AI agents, and the transition from simulation to real-world deployment.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design and implement decision-making pipelines that fuse multimodal sensor data to navigate unstructured environments. They will master advanced reinforcement learning techniques tailored for safety-critical autonomous systems, formulate probabilistic models for uncertainty quantification in dynamic scenarios, and evaluate agent performance under edge cases and adversarial conditions. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to translate theoretical AI concepts into practical solutions for robotics and self-driving vehicles while adhering to rigorous safety standards.

주차별 강의계획
Week 1: Introduction to Autonomous Systems & Decision-Making Frameworks
- Overview of autonomous driving stacks (Perception, Prediction, Planning, Control)
- Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) and Partially Observable MDPs (POMDPs)
- Case studies in robotic navigation and self-driving scenarios

Week 2: Multimodal Perception for Decision Making
- Sensor fusion architectures (Visual + LiDAR + Radar)
- Transformer-based models for cross-modal alignment
- Handling noisy and incomplete sensor data in real-time

Week 3: Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Agents
- Fundamentals of RL: Value functions, Policy gradients, Actor-Critic methods
- Deep Q-Networks (DQN) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
- Application to robotic manipulation tasks

Week 4: Safe and Sample-Efficient Learning
- Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs)
- Risk-sensitive RL and safety layers
- Sim-to-real transfer challenges and domain randomization techniques

Week 5: Planning under Uncertainty and Dynamics
- Model Predictive Control (MPC) integrated with learned dynamics models
- Probabilistic Roadmap (PRM) and Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) for path planning
- Collision avoidance strategies in dense traffic environments

Week 6: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for Reasoning
- Leveraging vision-language models for high-level task understanding
- Chain-of-thought reasoning in autonomous agents
- Generating natural language explanations for system decisions

Week 7: Ethical AI and Safety-Critical Systems
- Bias detection in multimodal datasets
- Explainable AI (XAI) for autonomous decision logs
- Regulatory frameworks and liability in autonomous accidents

Week 8: Project Proposal & Simulation Environment Setup
- Defining project scope: Autonomous driving vs. warehouse robotics
- Setting up simulation environments (e.g., CARLA, MuJoCo, Isaac Sim)
- Baseline model selection and evaluation metrics definition

Week 9: Advanced Topics: Multi-Agent Coordination
- Decentralized decision-making in multi-robot systems
- Communication protocols for agent collaboration
- Conflict resolution in shared spaces

Week 10: Real-World Deployment Challenges
- Edge computing constraints and latency optimization
- Continuous learning and system updates in the field
- Handling long-tail scenarios (corner cases)

Week 11: Midterm Project Presentation & Review
- Student progress reports on simulation-based prototypes
- Peer review of safety analysis methodologies
- Instructor feedback on architectural choices

Week 12: Final Project Implementation & Testing
- Integration of perception and planning modules
- Stress testing under adversarial conditions
- Documentation of failure modes and mitigation strategies

Week 13: Capstone Project Presentations
- Demonstration of autonomous agents in complex scenarios
- Discussion of ethical implications and future research directions
- Q&A session with industry experts

Week 14: Course Wrap-up & Future Trends
- Emerging trends in Decision-Making AI (e.g., world models, neuro-symbolic AI)
- Career paths in autonomous systems and robotics
- Final reflections on the societal impact of intelligent agents

detail.query: Theory of Computation (Computational Geometry, Graph Theory), Security for Critical Infrastructure, ICS Security, Wireless Sensor Networks에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
이산수학 및 알고리즘 설계 (CS305-01)
교과개요
This course explores the theoretical foundations of computation with a focus on discrete structures and algorithmic efficiency. Topics include graph theory, computational geometry, complexity classes (P, NP, etc.), and formal verification techniques. The curriculum bridges abstract mathematical concepts with practical applications in network security, critical infrastructure protection, and wireless sensor networks. Students will learn to model complex systems using graphs and geometric constraints, analyze the security properties of distributed protocols, and design algorithms that are both correct and efficient for resource-constrained environments.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate real-world problems in terms of graphs and geometric spaces, prove the computational complexity of proposed algorithms, and apply formal methods to verify the security of critical infrastructure systems. The course also aims to develop rigorous reasoning skills for analyzing distributed network behaviors and designing robust protocols for wireless sensor networks under adversarial conditions.

---

보안 및 신뢰성 공학 (CS410-01)
교과개요
This course addresses advanced challenges in securing cyber-physical systems, specifically targeting critical infrastructure and Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems. Utilizing concepts from the theory of computation, we examine vulnerabilities in wireless sensor networks and industrial control systems (ICS). The course covers formal security models, intrusion detection mechanisms, and resilience strategies against physical-cyber attacks. We will analyze how computational geometry can be used for spatial access control and how graph-theoretic approaches enhance network topology protection. Practical sessions focus on simulating attacks on critical infrastructure and developing countermeasures that maintain system availability and integrity.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to identify security flaws in distributed wireless sensor networks, design resilient architectures for critical infrastructure using graph-based redundancy, and apply formal verification techniques to ensure the correctness of safety-critical algorithms. The course also aims to foster an understanding of the trade-offs between computational efficiency and security guarantees in resource-limited environments, enabling students to lead the development of trustworthy embedded systems.

detail.query: Computer Vision, Multimodal AI, Physical AI, Medical AI에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Physical AI for Robotics (ME450-01)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of deep learning and physical laws to create intelligent agents that can interact safely and efficiently with the real world. Unlike traditional data-driven approaches that rely solely on massive datasets, this curriculum integrates differential equations, conservation laws, and geometric constraints directly into neural network architectures. Students will investigate how multimodal sensor inputs (vision, force, proprioception) can be fused to learn dynamic models of physical environments, enabling robust control in unstructured settings such as medical surgery or disaster response.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate physical constraints as differentiable layers within neural networks, design multimodal perception systems that align visual observations with physical dynamics, and develop simulation-to-real transfer strategies for robotic manipulation. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to critique existing AI models through the lens of physical plausibility and ethical safety in high-stakes domains like healthcare.

detail.lab: 컴파일러 및 런타임 시스템 연구실(Corus Lab)
detail.query: Compiler Optimization / Homomorphic Encryption Compiler /, GPU Compiler for AI/Graph / Domain-specific Compiler에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
컴파일러 최적화 및 도메인 특화 컴파일러 (Compiler Optimization / Domain-Specific Compiler)
교과개요
This course explores the advanced techniques and architectural challenges in building high-performance compilers for modern computing platforms. We will cover the full compilation pipeline from source code to optimized machine code, with a specific focus on graph-based optimization strategies, dataflow analysis, and resource-aware scheduling. The curriculum bridges theoretical compiler design with practical implementation, addressing critical issues in parallelism extraction, memory hierarchy management, and energy efficiency. Special attention is given to emerging domains such as GPU acceleration for AI workloads, homomorphic encryption execution environments, and hardware-specific instruction set architectures (ISA). Students will learn how to construct domain-specific compilers that automatically translate high-level mathematical models into efficient low-level code tailored for heterogeneous systems.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to design and implement compiler passes that effectively optimize complex computational graphs for both CPU and GPU architectures. They will gain proficiency in applying graph rewriting techniques, performing precise dataflow analysis, and managing memory layouts for large-scale matrix operations common in AI applications. Furthermore, students will develop the capability to create domain-specific intermediate representations (IR) and backend generators that support specialized hardware constraints, including those required for secure computation via homomorphic encryption. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of how compiler innovations directly impact performance, scalability, and energy consumption in next-generation computing systems.

---

GPU 컴파일러 및 AI 워크로드 최적화 (CS598-01)
교과개요
This intensive seminar focuses on the unique challenges of compiling and optimizing applications for Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) and other accelerators used in Artificial Intelligence. We will delve into the specifics of GPU architectures, including multi-level memory hierarchies, warp scheduling, and tensor core utilization. The course integrates concepts from graph theory to model computational dependencies and data movement patterns, which are essential for optimizing large-scale deep learning frameworks. Topics include automatic parallelization strategies, kernel fusion techniques, and the development of custom compilers that can handle irregular workloads often found in scientific computing and cryptographic applications like homomorphic encryption. Through hands-on projects, students will implement optimizations that reduce latency and increase throughput by aligning software abstractions with hardware capabilities.
교과목표
Upon completion, students will be equipped to analyze GPU performance bottlenecks and apply advanced compiler transformations such as loop tiling, vectorization, and memory coalescing to achieve near-peak hardware utilization. They will learn to construct domain-specific compilers that abstract away low-level hardware details while exposing sufficient control for fine-grained optimization of AI models. The course also emphasizes the ability to evaluate trade-offs between compilation time and runtime performance, ensuring that generated code is not only fast but also portable across different GPU generations. Ultimately, students will master the skills necessary to build compiler toolchains that enable efficient execution of complex graph-based computations on heterogeneous hardware platforms.

detail.query: Computer architecture / Resource disaggregation / Memory, security / Memory compression / Chiplet에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
컴퓨터 아키텍처 및 리소스 디애그리게이션 (Resource Disaggregation) 에 특화된 가상 강의계획서입니다. 요청하신 형식에 맞춰 작성되었습니다.

컴퓨터구조론 (전산시스템 최적화) (CS450-01)
교과개요
This course explores advanced paradigms in computer architecture with a specific focus on resource disaggregation, memory hierarchy optimization, and security-aware system design. We investigate techniques for decoupling compute, memory, and storage resources to enable flexible scaling and efficient multi-tenant environments. Special emphasis is placed on memory compression algorithms that minimize bandwidth overhead while maintaining data integrity, and the integration of hardware-based security mechanisms within disaggregated architectures. Furthermore, the course examines Chiplet-based design methodologies, analyzing how heterogeneous dies can be interconnected to overcome traditional monolithic scaling limits while addressing inter-chip communication latency and thermal challenges.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design resource-disaggregated system topologies that maximize utilization efficiency under varying workload patterns. Students will master advanced memory compression techniques to extend effective memory capacity without proportional power or bandwidth costs, and implement security protocols tailored for distributed memory pools. Additionally, learners will gain proficiency in evaluating Chiplet interconnect architectures (such as CXL and UCIe) to balance performance, cost, and security trade-offs in next-generation heterogeneous computing systems.

주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 리소스 디애그리게이션 개요 및 아키텍처 패러다임 전환
2 주차: 메모리 계층 구조와 대역폭 병목 현상 분석
3 주차: 메모리 압축 알고리즘 (Lossless/Lossy) 과 성능 영향도 평가
4 주차: 보안 강화된 분산 메모리 풀 설계 및 접근 제어
5 주차: Chiplet 기반 이종 칩 통합과 인터커넥트 기술 (CXL, UCIe)
6 주차: 이질적 다이 간 통신 지연 최소화 전략
7 주차: 열 관리와 전력 효율성 최적화
8 주차: 실제 사례 연구 - 클라우드 환경에서의 리소스 풀링 구현
9 주차: 보안 취약점 분석 및 하드웨어 기반 방호 기법
10 주차: Chiplet 설계 툴체인과 시뮬레이션 방법론
11 주차: 워크로드 특성에 따른 아키텍처 자동 구성 (Auto-tuning)
12 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 미래 컴퓨팅 트렌드 논의

detail.query: Data Mining / Query-Aware Data Systems /, Streaming & Adaptive Computation / Applied AI에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
데이터 마이닝 및 적응형 컴퓨팅 (BS305-01)
교과개요
This course explores advanced techniques for extracting meaningful patterns from high-dimensional and dynamic data streams.
Focusing on the intersection of Data Mining, Query-Aware Data Systems, and Streaming Computation, we examine how
systems can adapt to evolving query workloads in real-time without sacrificing performance or accuracy.
Students will investigate adaptive indexing strategies, online learning algorithms for concept drift detection,
and resource-aware query optimization techniques that leverage hardware heterogeneity. The curriculum bridges
theoretical foundations of statistical learning with practical implementations in distributed environments.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design scalable data mining pipelines capable of handling
continuous data streams, formulate query-aware system architectures that dynamically adjust to workload changes,
and apply adaptive computation methods to optimize resource utilization in AI-driven applications.
The course also aims to cultivate the ability to evaluate trade-offs between latency, throughput, and model accuracy
in real-world streaming scenarios.

This course bridges the gap between traditional programming language theory and the emerging demands of artificial intelligence. The curriculum covers type systems that ensure correctness in neural network code, optimization techniques for large-scale model training, and the integration of symbolic reasoning with deep learning. Students will gain hands-on experience building custom DSLs (Domain Specific Languages) to accelerate research in reinforcement learning, natural language processing, and computer vision.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design programming languages that natively support gradient-based optimization and backpropagation, implement efficient compilers for machine learning frameworks, and formally verify properties of AI models using advanced type theories. detail.query: Cryptography, Distributed Computing, Privacy Enhancing, Technologies에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
Privacy-Enhancing Cryptography for Distributed Systems (CSE450)
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of advanced cryptography and distributed computing, focusing on techniques that preserve data privacy in decentralized environments. We move beyond traditional encryption to examine protocols such as Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC), Homomorphic Encryption, and Zero-Knowledge Proofs. The curriculum emphasizes practical implementation challenges in large-scale networks, addressing how to perform computations on encrypted data without revealing underlying inputs or intermediate results. Students will analyze the trade-offs between computational efficiency, communication overhead, and security guarantees when deploying privacy-enhancing technologies in real-world distributed architectures.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to design cryptographic protocols that enable secure collaboration among untrusted parties in a distributed setting. They will gain proficiency in constructing and evaluating systems based on MPC and Homomorphic Encryption, ensuring robustness against various attack vectors including side-channel analysis and network failures. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to assess privacy risks in emerging distributed frameworks and propose innovative solutions that balance strong security guarantees with practical scalability.

---

Distributed Consensus and Privacy-Preserving Data Analytics (CSE460)
교과개요
This course investigates the fundamental challenges of achieving consensus and performing data analytics in distributed systems where data sensitivity is paramount. We delve into Byzantine fault-tolerant algorithms adapted for privacy constraints, exploring how to maintain system integrity without compromising user confidentiality. Topics include federated learning architectures, differential privacy mechanisms integrated with distributed databases, and secure aggregation protocols for cloud-edge collaboration. Through case studies of blockchain-based identity management and decentralized finance (DeFi) security, students will understand the theoretical underpinnings and practical deployment strategies for privacy-enhancing technologies in next-generation computing infrastructures.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate distributed algorithms that satisfy both consistency requirements and strict privacy budgets defined by differential privacy. They will apply secure aggregation techniques to build scalable analytics pipelines that prevent data leakage during model training or query execution. The course also aims to strengthen the ability to critically evaluate the security posture of distributed systems against sophisticated adversaries and communicate complex privacy-preserving design decisions effectively to technical stakeholders.

This course explores the frontier of next-generation electronic and photonic devices that transcend traditional silicon limitations. The curriculum bridges advanced semiconductor physics with emerging AI device architectures, emphasizing how novel materials and processing methods enable high-performance, low-power, and conformable electronic systems.

By the end of the course, students will be able to design concepts for disruptive electronic devices utilizing non-silicon materials, optimize optical fabrication processes for high-resolution nanostructures, and develop flexible/wearable platforms capable of integrating AI algorithms at the edge. This course bridges the gap between idealized circuit theory and practical silicon implementation, focusing on the design of high-performance analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits. RF 시스템 설계 및 에너지 효율 최적화 (EE490-01)
교과개요
This course focuses on the design of energy-efficient Radio Frequency Integrated Circuits (RFICs) tailored for wireless sensor nodes in biomedical and IoT applications. Utilizing advanced analog/mixed-signal techniques, students will explore low-power RF core circuit design, including low-noise amplifiers, mixers, oscillators, and power amplifiers optimized for battery-operated devices.
